correctness.rationale: The norm satisfies 4‖(x,y)‖²=5x²+2|xy|+y². After invertible diagonal normalization M(s,t)²=s²+t²+2|st|/√5, the whole sphere is four smooth elliptical arcs plus four nonsmooth axes. The two-dimensional Mizuguchi–Saito–Tanaka Birkhoff-frame characterization applies. Smooth tangent-line bounds yield frame M(x)≤√5/2. At the axis e=(1,0), one-sided subderivatives give the entire BJ cone |a|≤|b|/√5; normalization y_r=(r,1), 0≤r≤1/√5, covers it. Both exact upper-bound identities 8/5−q−(α+) and 8/5−q+(α−) were independently verified symbolically against their factorizations, with nonnegative numerators on the prescribed interval. Level subinterval containment at large radii for r>0, followed by r↓0, supplies the matching √(8/5) frame supremum. Thus DW=2√(8/5)=√(32/5), including boundary r=0 and nonsmooth axes.
residual_risks: The sharp frame value is a supremum approached from r>0, not claimed attained by one fixed axis tangent direction; no extension to ces_p or infinite dimensions.

The full 2013 BJ frame paper treats a distinct Day–James plane; the complete 2026 Alonso–Martín DW paper treats hexagon and other norms and not this Cesàro plane. Resultary searches recovered the current claim and distinct constants for ces_2 or ces_3, not a mathematical implication of √(32/5). Best-of-knowledge novelty with residual possibility of an older differently notated calculation.

value.rationale: The two-dimensional Cesàro space is a canonical low-dimensional benchmark in Banach-space geometry. Its exact ordinary Dunkl–Williams constant is a natural sharp norm-invariant absent from the known same-space James calculation; identifying nonsmooth-axis control instead of smooth elliptical maximizers gives a genuinely informative geometric boundary fact. No parameter-family theorem is demanded.
